acceptance_boundary: <Node> is accepted. Other notation is a proposal in an Analysis Draft; Current CFEL remains authoritative until source revisions and migration. Named participants and anonymous instance selectors as described are proposals, not adopted syntax.

findings.evidence: Current R2471 reads `Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF` as the named Relation instance; proposal reassigns // to broader-to-narrower inheritance. A1321 gives no named-instance form.
findings.impact: The same written expression can instead mean a narrower kind; exact IDs and Subject paths cannot be mapped or parsed safely until named-instance address syntax is chosen.

findings.evidence: Proposed Whole/Part and Broader//Narrower reverse the current / meaning; existing +>, <+, and R2609 reverse <((NAME)) have separate directional semantics. No reverse containment or narrower-to-broader spelling is proposed.
findings.impact: Both orientations and directional endpoint count positions must remain distinguishable; not a reason to change named Relation reverse syntax merely by analogy.

findings.evidence: $<Node> is proposed for an anonymous instance and $x[<Node>] for a named participant; Current R2471/R2243 distinguish identity, instance population and per-bearer counts.
findings.impact: Specify whether a constraint applies per matching instance or to the selected set, what repeated anonymous occurrences denote, and where {:n} counts attach. Do not infer that an anonymous selector creates an instance.

findings.evidence: [int, 0..100], $x[<Node>, .Header.Status = Active] and $n[int, 1+] reuse brackets for type and conditions; <Node> denotes a model kind. Current < is also a comparison and starts <((RELATION)) reverse.
findings.impact: Specify bracket element order, separators and relative condition bearer; delimit kind wrapping context so it cannot swallow or be confused with comparison/reverse syntax. This is a scoping/grammar concern, not proof that <Node> collides when delimited.

findings.topic: named reverse syntax and relational aliases
findings.evidence: R2609 defines Target <((RELATION)) Source; R2487/R2471 retain cardinality swap and no inverse permission from a reverse view. Proposal leaves reverse traversal open.
findings.impact: Do not interpret <(( as <kind>, or equate display reversal with a new authored inverse. Verify existing glyph/alias declarations together if changed.

findings.evidence: Current : admits values and {:n} marks an allowed cardinality; A1321 only proposes ~ for allowed values and gives /~ENGINE/... as a full path example.
findings.impact: Changing a value operator does not by itself change {:n}, selector :=, quoted text or ~ within a path. Separate contexts and lexical boundaries, especially a /~ path segment versus ~ operator.

findings.evidence: A1321 proposes explicit quantification and says IF must not silently introduce a participant; Current R2487 permits binding by IF membership and R2604 has an IF-local scope rule.
findings.impact: Source and instances relying on Current IF binding need reviewed migration; FOR EACH is candidate only. No loop or mutable-variable semantics follows.

top_question.question: With `//` reserved for narrowing, how should we write a named instance such as the existing `Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF` so it is distinguishable from a narrower kind?
top_question.example: Current `Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF` = the named Relation instance; proposed `Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF` would read as a narrower kind. What should the named instance address become?
top_question.impact: All authored named-instance references, relation declarations, Subject identity and migration depend on this choice; a guess can change the addressed Entity.

routine_details: Whitespace and line-break formatting can follow a subsequently specified grammar; do not block the conceptual choice.
Examples do not imply Runtime implementation, parsing, executable I/O, or automatic writes.
No assumption that every < character denotes a kind; token context must be specified.
boundary: Read-only source analysis; no parser/code/tests, Current, actual Draft, Workflow/Workbench or Git mutations.
